questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding mixtures?

options.text: Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures in which the particle size is large.
The major component of a solution is called the solvent.
The minor component of a solution is called the solute.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures in which the particle size is large **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A mixture is a combination of two or more substances that are not chemically bonded to each other.
 
• Mixtures can be classified into two types: homogeneous and heterogeneous.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition throughout, whereas heterogeneous mixtures have a non-uniform composition.
 
• The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, distillation, chromatography, etc.
 
• Filtration is used to separate a solid from a liquid or a gas.
 
• Distillation is used to separate a mixture of two or more liquids with different boiling points.
 
• **Colloids**, also known as colloidal solutions or colloidal systems, are mixtures in which microscopically dispersed insoluble particles of one substance are suspended in another substance. 
 
• The size of the suspended particles in a colloid can range from 1 to 1000 nanometres (10-9 meters) which is **very small**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Solution **

 
• A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances, where one substance is called the solute and the other is called the solvent.
 
• The solute is the substance that is dissolved in the solvent, whereas the solvent is the substance in which the solute is dissolved.
 
• Solutions can be classified as solid, liquid, or gaseous, depending on the physical state of the solvent.
 
• The concentration of a solution is the amount of solute present in a given amount of solvent or solution.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.text: Animal cells do not have plastids.
Plant cells have cell walls, whereas animal cells do not.
Plant cells are generally larger than animal cells.
Plant cells have smaller vacuoles than those of animal cells.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** option 4**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Actually, plant cells typically have **much larger vacuoles** than animal cells.
 
• These vacuoles serve various functions in plant cells, including storing water, nutrients, and waste products.
 
• They also help maintain cell turgor (internal pressure).
 
• In contrast, animal cells have smaller vacuoles or none at all, and their functions are primarily related to cellular waste removal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **It is True.**

 
 
• Plastids are organelles found in plant cells that are responsible for photosynthesis and other functions
 
• Animal cells do not need these organelles as they do not perform photosynthesis.
 
 
 
 
 
• ** Plant cells have cell walls, whereas animal cells do not.**
 
 
• **It is ****True.**
 
 
• Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides structural support and protection.
 
• Animal cells lack a cell wall, but they have a flexible cell membrane.
 
 
 
 
 
• ** Plant cells are generally larger than animal cells.**
 
 
• **It is True.**
 
 
• **​** Plant cells are often larger than animal cells due to the presence of a large central vacuole.
 
• This vacuole occupies most of the cell's volume and helps to maintain cell turgor.

questions.question: The speed of a bus increases by 4 km/hr after every one hour. If the distance travelled in the first one hour was 55 km, then what was the total distance travelled in 13 hours?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of car increases after every hour = 4 km / h

Distance travelled in 1st one hour = 55 km

Formula used :

Sum of n terms of an AP = n/2[2a + (n - 1)d]

AP = Arithmetic progression 

**Calculation:**

Distance travelled in 2nd hour = 55 + 4 = 59 km

Distance travelled in 3rd hour 59 + 4 = 63 km

Distance travelled by car in every hour will be in AP 

55, 59, 63 ... up to 13 terms. 

First term = a = 55, common difference = d = 59 - 55 = 4,

Number of terms = n = 13

Total distance travelled in 13 hours = 13 / 2 [ 2 x 55 + ( 13 - 1 ) 4 ] 

⇒ 13 / 2 ( 110 + 48 )

⇒ 13 × 79 = 1027 km

**Hence, the total distance travelled in 13 hours is 1027 km.**

questions.question: Shadows are formed when __________ objects come in the path of light.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**opaque**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Opaque objects** are those that do not allow light to pass through them.
 
• When light encounters an opaque object, it is either absorbed or reflected, but not transmitted.
 
• This interaction of light with opaque objects results in the formation of **shadows**.
 
• Shadows are areas where light is blocked by the opaque object, creating a dark shape on a surface opposite the light source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Luminous objects** are those that emit their own light, such as the sun or a light bulb.
 
• **Transparent objects** allow light to pass through them completely, like clear glass or clean water.
 
• **Translucent objects** allow some light to pass through but scatter it, such as frosted glass or thin paper.
 
• The study of light and shadows is a fundamental aspect of physics, specifically in the branch of optics.

questions.question: A team of 30 men is supposed to complete a work in 41 days. After 25 days, 6 more men are employed, and the work is finished one day earlier. By how many days would it have been delayed, if 6 more men were not employed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the work finished 1 day earlier than the 41-day schedule, it finished in 40 days.

The remaining work after 25 days was completed by 36 men in 15 days (40 − 25 = 15).

Total remaining work = 36 × 15 = 540 man-days.

If only the original 30 men worked, time taken for remaining work = 540 ÷ 30 = 18 days.

Initial scheduled time for the remaining work = 41 − 25 = 16 days.

Delay = Time taken by 30 men − Scheduled time = 18 − 16 = 2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men = 30

Scheduled time to complete work = 41 days

Number of days worked by 30 men = 25 days

Extra men added after 25 days = 6

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Men × Number of Days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Actual time taken to finish the work = 41 − 1 = 40 days

⇒ Days worked by the new group of men = 40 − 25 = 15 days

⇒ Total men working in the last 15 days = 30 + 6 = 36 men

⇒ Remaining work completed by 36 men = 36 × 15 = 540 units

⇒ If no extra men were added, time taken by 30 men to complete 540 units = 540 ÷ 30 = 18 days

⇒ Total days taken if no extra men were added = 25 + 18 = 43 days

⇒ Delay = Total days taken − Scheduled days

⇒ Delay = 43 − 41 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

For a group of men working, the relation between Men (M), Days (D), Hours (H) and Work (W) is given by: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Efficiency & Time Relationship

The efficiency of a worker is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. If efficiency ratio of A and B is x:y, their time taken ratio will be y:x.

Total Work Formula

Total work can be assumed as the LCM of the days taken by individuals, and it is calculated as Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken.

Different techniques are used to separate mixtures based on the physical and chemical properties of the components.

**1. Sublimation:** This process is used to separate a mixture of substances where one of them can turn directly from the solid state to the gaseous state without becoming liquid. An example of such a substance is napthalene.

**2. Crystallisation: **This method is used to purify substances. It's usually employed to separate solids that have dissolved in a liquid and need to be recovered.

**3. Evaporation: **This process is used to separate a soluble substance from a solution. It is usually used to separate a solid substance that has dissolved in a liquid and needs to be retrieved.

**4. Separating Funnel: **This method is typically used to separate two immiscible liquids. Immiscible liquids are those that do not mix to form a homogeneous mixture. An example is oil and water.

** __Explanation__: **

(A) **Powdered napthalene balls and salt:** Napthalene sublimates, so the method to separate this mixture would be sublimation (III).

(B) **Sugar and water: **Sugar dissolves in water to form a homogeneous mixture. It can be separated by crystallisation (I), which will allow the sugar to form crystals that can be removed from the water.

(C)** Vegetable oil and water:** These are two immiscible liquids. They can be separated using a separating funnel (IV), which allows the denser liquid (water) to be drained off from the bottom.

(D) **Salt and water:** Salt dissolves in water and can be retrieved through evaporation (II). The water is evaporated, leaving the salt behind.

questions.question: A train left 4 hours early than the scheduled time and in order to reach its destination 960 km away on time, it had to decrease its usual speed by 40 km/hr. What is the usual speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 960 km

Train left 4 hours early

Decrease in speed = 40 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the usual speed be S km/hr.

Usual time to cover the distance = 960 / S

New speed = (S - 40) km/hr

New time to cover the distance = 960 / (S - 40)

Since the train left 4 hours early and reached on time:

New time - Usual time = 4 hours

⇒ 960 / (S - 40) - 960 / S = 4

⇒ 960S - 960(S - 40) = 4S(S - 40)

⇒ 960S - 960S + 38400 = 4S² - 160S

⇒ 38400 = 4S² - 160S

⇒ 4S² - 160S - 38400 = 0

⇒ S² - 40S - 9600 = 0

Solving the quadratic equation:

S = +120 or -80

Since speed cannot be negative, S = 120 km/hr

**The usual speed of the train is 120 km/hr.**

questions.question: The chemical formula of glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆. The weight % of carbon in glucose is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**40%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical formula for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
• The molar mass of glucose can be calculated by summing the molar masses of its constituent elements: Carbon (C), Hydrogen (H), and Oxygen (O).
 
• To find the percentage of carbon in glucose, the mass of carbon atoms in one mole of glucose is divided by the molar mass of glucose and then multiplied by 100.
 
• This gives the weight percentage of carbon in glucose as 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Formula**

 
 
• The molecular formula of a compound gives the exact number of atoms of each element in a molecule of the compound.
 
• For glucose, the molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass**
 
 
• The molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance (chemical element or chemical compound).
 
• The molar masses of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen are approximately 12 g/mol, 1 g/mol, and 16 g/mol, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Percentage Composition by Mass**
 
 
• The percentage composition by mass of an element in a compound is the percentage by mass of that element in the compound.
 
• It is calculated as (mass of the element in 1 mole of the compound / molar mass of the compound) × 100.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Weight % of Carbon in Glucose**
 
 
• The molar mass of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) = (6 × 12) + (12 × 1) + (6 × 16) = 180 g/mol.
 
• The mass of carbon in one mole of glucose = 6 × 12 = 72 g.
 
• Weight % of carbon in glucose = (72 g / 180 g) × 100 = 40%.

__
 
• Work is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• Here, the force applied is **7 N**, and the displacement is **5 m**.
 
• If the force and displacement are in the same direction, cos(θ) = cos(0°) = 1.
 
• Thus, Work = 7 × 5 × 1 = **35 J**.
 
• The unit of work in the SI system is the **joule (J)**.

• Work is done when a force is applied to an object, and the object moves in the direction of the force.
 
• It is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• The formula for work (W) is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where:
 
 
• F = Force applied (N)
 
• d = Displacement (m)
 
• θ = Angle between the force and displacement
 
 
 
 
 
• **Joule:**
 
 
• The joule (J) is the SI unit of work and energy.
 
• **1 joule is equivalent to 1 newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• It represents the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Work:**
 
 
• The magnitude of the force applied.
 
• The displacement caused by the force.
 
• The angle between the force and the displacement.

F=B × I × L × sin(θ)

__
 
• B is the magnitude of the magnetic field (in Tesla, T)
 
• I is the current flowing through the wire (in Amperes, A)
 
• L is the length of the wire segment in the magnetic field (in meters, m)
 
• θ is the angle between the current direction and the magnetic field direction

Given:

I=8 A

B=0.15 T

θ=30 degrees

We need to find the force per unit length, so we'll ignore the length (L) as it cancels out when we're calculating force per unit length.

 F = 0.15 · 8 · sin 30° = 0.6 {N m}⁻¹ 

So, the magnitude of the magnetic force per unit length on the wire is **0.6N/m.**__

questions.question: Two cubes, each having the length of each side as 8 cm, are joined to form a cuboid. What will be the total surface area of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of the cubes = 8 cm

**Concept used:**

Total surface area of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Here,

h = height

b = breadth

l = length

**Calculation:**

After joining two cubes length of the formed cuboid will be = 8 + 8

⇒ 16 cm

Height and breadth of the formed cuboid will be 8 cm

Now,

Total surface area of the formed cuboid = 2(16 × 8 + 16 × 8 + 8 × 8)

⇒ 2(128 + 128 + 64)

⇒ 2 × 320

⇒ 640

So, total surface area of the cuboid = 640 cm²

**∴ The total surface area of the cuboid will be 640 cm2.**

questions.question: P sells a toy to Q at a profit of 40 percent and Q sells it to R at a profit of 10 percent. If R pays Rs. 539 for the toy, then what was the cost price of toy for P?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P sold the toy to Q at 40% profit

Q sold it to R at 10% profit

R paid Rs. 539 for the toy

**Formula used:**

Profit percent = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

**Solution:**

⇒ Selling Price of Q to R = Rs. 539

⇒ Cost Price for Q = Selling Price of Q to R / (1 + profit% of Q) = 539/1.1

⇒ Cost Price for P = Cost Price for Q/(1 + profit% of P)

**Therefore, the cost price of the toy for P is Rs. 350 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 539 = CP of P × 140/100 × 110/100

⇒ CP of P = (539 × 100)/(14 × 11) = Rs. 350

∴ The cost price of the toy for P is Rs. 350.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-contact force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gravitational force is an attractive force that acts between any two masses.
 
• This force is described by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation, which states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points.
 
• The magnitude of the gravitational force between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• Gravitational force does not require any physical contact between the objects; it acts over a distance.
 
• This force is responsible for keeping the planets in orbit around the sun and for the phenomenon of objects falling to the ground when dropped.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Friction**

 
 
• Friction is a force that opposes the relative motion or tendency of such motion of two surfaces in contact.
 
• It acts parallel to the surfaces and opposite to the direction of motion.
 
• Frictional forces can be divided into static friction, which prevents motion, and kinetic friction, which opposes ongoing motion.
 
• The magnitude of the frictional force depends on the nature of the surfaces and the normal force pressing them together.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/def261f2f67324b43ed5f4da5a1abfae79c2f804b90e0742bb3a26c787133322.png] 

 
• **Normal Force**

 
 
• The normal force is the perpendicular force exerted by a surface on an object in contact with it.
 
• This force prevents objects from "falling" into whatever they are in contact with.
 
• The magnitude of the normal force is equal to the component of the object's weight perpendicular to the contact surface.
 
• It acts in a direction perpendicular to the surface of contact.
 
 
 
• **Tension Force**
 
 
• Tension is a force that is transmitted through a string, rope, cable or wire when it is pulled tight by forces acting from opposite ends.
 
• The tension force is directed along the length of the wire and pulls equally on the objects on the opposite ends of the wire.
 
• Tension always pulls and never pushes.
 
• The magnitude of tension depends on the forces acting at the ends of the cable and the mass of the cable itself.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Force**
 
 
• Electromagnetic force is a type of physical interaction that occurs between electrically charged particles.
 
• This force can be attractive or repulsive depending on the charges of the interacting particles.
 
• It is responsible for phenomena such as electricity, magnetism, and light.
 
• The electromagnetic force is one of the four fundamental forces of nature, along with gravitational, strong nuclear, and weak nuclear forces.
